title: Google Assistant Is Being Switched Off
hook: The voice you've been telling to set timers since 2016 is going away. Google plans to shut Assistant off on phones on September 4, leaving Gemini as the only way to talk to your Android.
key_points: Ars Technica reports Google plans to end Assistant on phones on September 4.
Gemini, Google's newer AI model, becomes the sole voice-control option.
Assistant ran mostly on fixed commands; Gemini is a conversational language model.
Expect a trade: better conversation and reasoning, but different habits and quirks.
Simple routines you rely on — timers, alarms, smart lights — may need re-learning.
content_html: Google is retiring Assistant on phones — Ars Technica reports the shutdown is planned for September 4, after which Gemini becomes the only built-in way to control an Android device by voice. If you have said "Hey Google" to a phone in the last decade, you have been talking to Assistant.
extra_html: The switch is a good illustration of how AI has changed under the hood. Assistant was largely a command matcher: it listened for phrasings it recognized — set a timer, play this song, turn off the lights — and did the matching action. Gemini is a large language model, which means it generates its answer rather than looking it up, and can follow a rambling, multi-part request that Assistant would have refused. The cost of that flexibility is predictability. Fixed commands you have used for years may be interpreted slightly differently, and a model that improvises is a model that can occasionally improvise wrongly. For most people the practical advice is small: expect a few weeks of relearning phrasings, and re-check anything you had automated — routines, alarms, smart-home shortcuts — rather than assuming it survived the transition.

related.title: Siri Gets Rebuilt as a Real Assistant
related.hook: After years of promises, Apple unveiled 'Siri AI' — an 'entirely new version' that's more conversational and can handle messy tasks, like turning a flyer into calendar events. It's now in public beta.

related.title: Voice Assistants
related.hook: Siri and Alexa could set a timer; the new voice AIs can hold a real conversation. Talking is becoming a normal way to use AI — handy, natural, and always a little bit listening.

flashcards.prompt: What's the basic difference between Google Assistant and Gemini?
flashcards.back_html: Assistant mostly matched what you said against a fixed list of commands. Gemini is a conversational language model — it handles messier, open-ended requests, but behaves less predictably on rote ones.

flashcards.prompt: Why might swapping Assistant for Gemini feel like a downgrade at first, even if the AI is smarter?

choices.text: Habits built on fixed, predictable commands stop working the same way
Gemini cannot understand speech, only typing
Voice control will require a paid subscription for everyone

flashcards.explanation_html: A command-matching assistant is dependably literal. A language model is more capable and more variable, so long-memorized phrasings may need relearning.
